core: Crude birth rate (CBR) and crude death rate (CDR): definition as events per 1,000 people per year
Natural increase and the rate of natural increase (RNI = CBR - CDR, migration excluded)
Total fertility rate (TFR) and the ~2.1 replacement level
World population size (~8 billion, 8 billion reached 15 November 2022; ~8.2 billion in 2024) and that global growth is slowing
Age structure and the population pyramid: expansive vs stationary vs constrictive/contractive shapes

Global TFR of about 2.3 in 2024, down from over 5 in the 1960s

Population aging as fertility falls and life expectancy rises

claims.claim: The crude birth rate and crude death rate are the number of births (or deaths) per 1,000 people in a population in a given year.
The rate of natural increase equals the crude birth rate minus the crude death rate and excludes migration.

The total fertility rate is the average number of children a woman would have over her lifetime at current age-specific birth rates; a TFR of about 2.1 is replacement level, the rate that keeps a population stable over time ignoring migration, with the margin above 2 accounting for child mortality.
The world's population reached 8 billion on 15 November 2022, per the United Nations.

The world's population was about 8.2 billion in 2024 and is projected to peak at approximately 10.3 billion around the mid-2080s (2084) before declining slightly, per UN World Population Prospects 2024.

Global population growth is slowing: the annual growth rate peaked at over 2% (about 2.3%) in the 1960s and has fallen to under 1% (about 0.9% in 2023), and the global fertility rate fell from over 5 children per woman in the 1960s to about 2.3 in 2024.
It took 12 years for world population to grow from 7 to 8 billion but is projected to take about 15 years (to 2037) to reach 9 billion, a sign the growth rate is slowing.

Age structure is commonly shown as a population pyramid; an expansive pyramid has a broad base (young, high-birth-rate, rapidly growing population), a stationary pyramid has roughly even age groups (low birth and death rates), and a constrictive/contractive pyramid has a narrow base (low birth rates, aging population).
The world's population is aging as life expectancy rises and fertility falls, and by 2024 about one in four people lived in a country or area whose population had already peaked.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Exact projected peak size and timing vary by projection revision.
positions: UN WPP 2024: peak ~10.3 billion around 2084 (mid-2080s), then slight decline
Earlier revisions placed the peak later in the century and higher
conflictingEvidence.resolution: Cite the UN WPP 2024 figure with its year and describe it as a projection, not a certainty; note that projections are revised as fertility data change.

Supports world population ~8.2 billion in 2024, projected peak ~10.3 billion around the mid-2080s (2084), global TFR ~2.3 in 2024 down from over 5 in the 1960s, population aging, and one in four people living in a country whose population had already peaked. Figures cross-checked against the UN Global Issues page and OWID's 2024 revision analysis; used as reference only, prose written original.

Used to date the 8-billion milestone precisely.
